authored.note: Explanations are written for learners. Facts are checked word for word against the cited files. The evidence in Practice is read from the committed specimen packs, unedited.

summary.text: One agent asks another to act for it. The deputy may be able to do more than the caller was ever allowed to ask for. Three recorded runs show a legitimate delegation, the same extra request let through by an intentionally weak profile, and the same request refused by the defended profile.
facts: the deputy may possess authority, but that is not proof the caller delegated that authority for this operation.

glance.label: The legitimate operation
glance.text: Credit Agent asks Compliance Agent to perform a granted policy lookup, and the caller really did delegate it.
facts: A guided lab: Credit Agent asks Compliance Agent to perform an MCP tool call.

glance.label: What the attacker controls
glance.text: The operation requested through the deputy. The deputy has authority of its own that the caller does not.
facts: the deputy uses its own ambient authority for an operation the caller was not entitled to request.

glance.label: The trust boundary
glance.text: Between what the caller delegated and what the deputy could do on its own. A delegation check runs before the tool check.
facts: CTRL-DELEGATION-001 checks whether the caller actually delegated that operation.

glance.label: The authorization rule
glance.text: An agent cannot receive more authority than was explicitly delegated to it.
facts: an agent cannot receive more authority than was explicitly delegated.

glance.label: What counts as evidence of execution
glance.text: A decision is not execution. Look for the separate event that says the handler began.
facts: Treat runtime handler count as authoritative non-execution proof.

known.text: In the attack run the delegation check let the request through under the vulnerable profile. The lab calls this fail-open, not a grant from the caller.
facts: Explain why ATTACK CTRL-DELEGATION-001 ALLOW is fail-open, not caller grant.
